 Nebraska in the national news: October 2026
 November 2, 2026
 Nebraska in the national news: October 2026 
 By
 Sean Hagewood | University Communication and Marketing 
 Kristen Labadie | University Communication and Marketing 
 Kristen Labadie | University Communication and Marketing
 University of Nebraska–Lincoln political scientists were featured in a pair of prominent national news stories about the midterm election in October. The stories were among 25-plus featuring Husker faculty, staff, students, centers and programs during the month.
 Kevin Smith , Leland J. and Dorothy H. Olson Professor of political science, was a featured guest in the Oct. 5 episode of WAMU’s “If You Can Keep It,” which focused on the intersection between politics and mental health. He discussed his collaborative research on how politics affects well-being. “The key thing that we found is that an astonishing number of Americans say that politics is affecting their health broadly construed, not just their psychological health, but their social health and even their physical health.” He pointed to the repeated survey finding that one in 20 Americans say they have had suicidal thoughts because of politics. The episode was picked up by dozens of NPR affiliates nationwide. Smith was also interviewed for election-related stories in KETV , KLKN and Nebraska Public Media ( 1 , 2 ).
 Dona-Gene Barton , associate professor of political science, was interviewed for an Oct. 17 Newsweek article on the U.S. Senate race between incumbent Republican Sen. Pete Ricketts and independent challenger Dan Osborn. Barton said that a narrow advantage for Osborn in a recent YouGov survey shouldn’t be mistaken for an established trend. “One poll is a snapshot, not a trend,” she said. “I would caution against reading too much into a narrow lead that falls within the margin of error.” Geoff Lorenz, associate professor of political science, was also interviewed for an Oct. 17 Nebraska Examiner article on the hotly contested race.
 Additional national news coverage in October included:
 Many rural Nebraskans use trails around their communities and receive different benefits from their use, according to the 2026 Nebraska Rural Poll . Stories on the results appeared in KOLN/KGIN , Rural Radio Network and the Yankton (South Dakota) Daily Press and Dakotan .
 Guillermo Balboa , agronomy and horticulture, interim director of the new Nebraska Digital Agriculture Hub , was interviewed about the hub for an Oct. 6 segment on RFD-TV’s “Market Day Report.” The hub is bringing researchers, extension specialists and producers together to develop and test digital tools for agriculture.
 Researchers with the university’s Soybean Pathology Lab are taking their work beyond small research plots and into farmers’ fields, examining how diseases, varieties, seed treatments and environmental conditions interact on a field-scale level. Farm Journal’s Ag Web published an Oct. 6 article on the lab’s work. Dylan Mangel , extension soybean pathologist; Bhanu Dangi , field research technologist with the lab; and Olivia Dooley , a master’s student in the lab, were interviewed for the article.
 Dylan Lukken , a sophomore finance major from Dakota Dunes, South Dakota, and Annie Baumann , a junior nutrition and health sciences major from Yankton, South Dakota, are among 50 Husker students who have been selected for the Undergraduate Certificate in Sales Excellence Program in the College of Business, the Yankton Daily Press and Dakotan reported Oct. 6. With the credential offered by the Center for Sales Excellence , students sharpen communication, problem-solving and decision-making skills sought by employers.
 Brian Petrotta , sports media and communications, was interviewed for an Oct. 7 Montgomery County (Maryland) Sentinel article on female athletes facing online harassment. He attributed part of the problem to the media’s normalization of sports betting. “What’s really interesting is how quickly it happened,” he said. “We went from decades of something that, at least in mainstream journalism, we don’t talk about … and now it’s pretty well integrated into every aspect.”
 Farms.com ran an Oct. 8 article on 13 notable figures from the University of Nebraska–Lincoln who have shaped agricultural science and policymaking on a national scale.
 Brad Lubben , extension associate professor of agricultural economics, was interviewed for an Oct. 14 Brownfield Ag News article titled “Why higher farm safety net payments may not improve farm profitability.” “The margins are just as tight or even more challenging now in spite of the fact the safety net is at higher levels,” he said.
 Nipuna Chamara , biological systems engineering, was quoted in an Oct. 15 Newsweek article on the growing use of artificial intelligence agents in agriculture. “An AI agent can synthesize agronomic, soil, weather, imagery, machinery and economic data; evaluate alternative scenarios; and translate them into an actionable management recommendation such as when and how much to irrigate based on both crop need and profitability,” he said.
 Brock Ortner , a livestock extension educator with Nebraska Extension, was quoted in an Oct. 16 Harvest Public Media story on American hay growers facing a “triple whammy” of drought, pests and high fuel costs. He said few of the ranchers he works with had extra hay stowed away, which has led to elevated prices.
 New research from the University of Nebraska–Lincoln , Ohio State University and the University of Tennessee suggests that a farmers’ social network — not just agronomy or economics — determines whether soil health practices such as cover crops or no-till farming survive beyond their first season. Scienmag published an Oct. 16 article on the research.
 A Nebraska Water Center team has received a three-year, $496,722 National Science Foundation grant to investigate an understudied reservoir of organic nitrogen that may shape groundwater quality long after nitrogen management strategies are in place. A separate five-year, $570,000-plus award from the Nebraska Corn Board will help the researchers evaluate approaches that may proactively reduce nitrate risk before it reaches groundwater. The Fence Post and Tri-State Livestock News ran articles on the research.
 American School and University published an Oct. 17 story on Architecture Hall’s HDR Pavilion , which opened in fall 2024. The four-story, 21,252-square-foot addition features mass timber and includes 14 new design studios, a student lounge, critique spaces and areas for collaboration.
 The university has awarded stipends to 172 Husker undergraduates to participate in research with a faculty mentor during the fall and spring semesters. Nebraska’s Undergraduate Creative Activities and Research Experience program supports undergraduates to work with faculty mentors in research or creative activities. The Columbus Telegram , Minden Courier and Powell (Wyoming) Tribune ran articles on UCARE participants from their areas.
 Jordan Wicks , assistant professor of animal science and meats extension specialist, was interviewed for an Oct. 20 segment on RFD-TV’s “Market Day Report.” She discussed the flat iron steak, which is celebrating its 25th anniversary this year. University of Nebraska–Lincoln research helped bring the cut to consumers.
 Rural Radio Network , Farms.com and The Fence Post ran articles on Spur Ventures , a University of Nebraska–Lincoln initiative, and its AgConverge conference , set for Nov. 17-18 in Grand Island. Spur Ventures aims to connect producers, startups, industry, investors and students to accelerate the development, validation and commercialization of agricultural technologies.
 Millions of plastic bags have given an old road in South Sioux City a new look thanks to the expertise of Jamilla Teixeira , civil and environmental engineering, and a $500,000 grant from the Nebraska Environmental Trust. In June 2025, the city paved a 4,000-foot stretch of Foundry Road near Siouxland Freedom Park using a cutting-edge asphalt blend made from 2 million recycled plastic bags. Construction Equipment Guide published a front-page article on the project in its Oct. 24 print edition.
 Kait Chapman , an urban entomologist with Nebraska Extension, was interviewed for an Oct. 26 Yahoo article on a growing number of parents pushing back on schools easing their “no lice” policies. Treatment is a multistep process, said Chapman, who frequently works with early childhood education centers to teach them how to prevent and manage head lice. When she hears of cases where infestations are happening repeatedly, her first thought is that treatment wasn’t done correctly or completely.
 Cheryl Fitzgarrald, a Husker alumna from Omaha, claimed her missing wedding ring from the University of Nebraska–Lincoln Police Department’s lost and found after a friend from church told her about reading a recent Lincoln Journal Star article on the ring. The wedding band was discovered outside the Nebraska Union on Sept. 5 and turned over to University Police the next day. The Journal Star and UPI published articles on the ring finding its way home.
 Leadership and strategic visioning by Mary-Grace Danao , food science and technology and biological systems engineering, have helped position the University of Nebraska–Lincoln at the forefront of high pressure processing safety research, in partnership with private industry. Tri-State Livestock News ran an Oct. 27 article on the HPP work of Danao’s lab.
 Luke Satkus of Peoria, Arizona, is among 34 first-year students selected for the sixth cohort of the Integrity in Business Leadership program in the College of Business, the Peoria Independent reported Oct. 27. Satkus, who is majoring in international business, joins students representing eight states and 13 majors.
 The university’s Soil Judging Team recently finished fifth at the Region V Collegiate Soil Judging Contest in southern Missouri, Nebraska Ag Connection reported Oct. 27. Representing the team were Lara Arnold , Sydney Honaker , Lauren Rice , Diego Sanchez and Fionna Wynn . The team is coached by Becky Young .
 Faculty, administration, student and staff appearances in the national media are logged at  http://newsroom.unl.edu/inthenews . If you have additions to the list, contact Sean Hagewood at  shagewood2@unl.edu  or 402-472-8514. If you have suggestions for national news stories, email Deann Gayman at  deann.gayman@unl.edu .
